title: Smooth-functorial normalized resolution rules on rational finite-type inputs
statement:
Let a reduced finite-type rational input $X$ mean a scheme with structure morphism $q:X\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Q$, with $X$ reduced and $q$ locally of finite type and quasi-compact, as in [def-trf-ordinary-resolution-rule]. Its normal subtype consists of those inputs whose local rings are integrally closed domains [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Empty schemes and finite disjoint unions are allowed, with no separation or equidimensionality restriction.

For any family $I$ of schemes $b:I\to\mathit{Sch}$, a smooth-functorial normalized resolution rule assigns to every input a finite based normalized resolution tower and to every smooth morphism $h:b(Y)\to b(X)$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] the recursively pulled-back tower with its ordered unit-center contraction. The based tower and comparison data are those of [def-per-qe-normalized-resolution-rule]: coherent nonempty nowhere dense centers, a regular terminal scheme, a cartesian square at every level, extended center ideals and commuting arrows, deletion of exactly unit-center stages, each of which is an isomorphism, and preservation of the other center ideals in order. The empty input has length zero. The comparison indices and actual level maps respect identities and composition. For surjective smooth morphisms the contraction index is injective, hence no stage is deleted. The families used here are all reduced finite-type rational inputs and their normal subtype.

source.place: Expose VIII, 2.2.5--2.2.9 and 2.3.2--2.3.5, pp.90--92; smooth input-rule hypothesis of the conductor-prepending refinement.
